To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the COX 1 and COX 2 inhibitors, celecoxib and indomethacin, respectively, and the mTOR inhibitor, rapamycin, are effective in inhibiting cell growth and promoting apoptosis in melanoma cell lines in vitro.
celecoxib and mTOR inhibition by rapamycin inhibit malignant melanoma growth and that celecoxib has proapoptotic effect.
celecoxib and the mammalian rapamycin are both effective inhibitors of melanoma cell growth and that the combined use of both agents may be more effective than the use of either one alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new treatment strategies for metastasised malignant skin cancer.
the effects of celecoxibs and rapamycins on cell growth and the apoptosis of melanoma cells.
the development of a novel therapeutic approach for the palliative treatment of metastasised cutaneous malignant melanoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

both celecoxib (and probably other selective COX 2 inhibitors) and rapamycin (and probably other mTOR inhibitors) inhibit cell proliferation and induce apoptosis in malignant melanomas, and that the combination of both drugs has additive antitumor properties.
the COX 1 and 2 inhibitors are not only effective against the cancer cells themselves but also against cancer stem cells.
celecoxib and/or rapamycin should be considered as potential therapeutic options for patients with advanced malignant melanoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
celecoxib and/or rapamycin should be used as single agents in metastasised malignant skin melanoma.
both rapamycin and COX 2 inhibitors are effective drugs in the treatment of malignant melanoma.
the COX 1 and 2 expression is not a predictive marker for response to celecoxib in melanoma.

the COX-2 inhibitor celecoxb is a potent inhibitor of cell growth in melanoma cells and that the antiproliterative and proapopotic effect of celecoxib is independent of the COx-2 expression.
